title: The MOSFET as a Switch: How a Voltage Opens a Channel
topic: NMOS as a digital switch — when V_GS is below the threshold V_t the channel is empty and the transistor is off; raise V_GS above V_t and a conducting channel forms, dropping R_DS and turning the transistor on. Wire it as an inverter and the output flips with the input.

beats.narration: One voltage at the gate decides whether current flows from drain to source. Meet the MOSFET as a switch.

elements.content: One pin opens or closes the channel — meet the MOSFET as a switch.

beats.narration: An n channel MOSFET has three terminals — gate, drain and source. Between drain and source sits a slice of silicon that conducts only when a channel of electrons forms underneath the gate.

elements.content: NMOS symbol — drain on top, source on bottom, gate on left, body line with arrow
G, D, S labels next to terminals
Cross-section to the right — n+ source, n+ drain, p-substrate, gate over oxide, channel region empty
no electrons in the channel — drain and source are isolated

beats.narration: Push V G S past the threshold V t and electrons get pulled up into the channel. Now drain to source is a conducting path and the drain current jumps from zero up to its on value.

elements.content: Cross-section with V_GS slider above gate — sweeps from 0 to high; channel fills with charge dots once V_GS > V_t
I_D vs V_GS plot on the right — the I_D curve traces in as the cursor sweeps
V_t threshold tick on the V_GS axis
below V_t — channel empty, no current. Above V_t — channel forms, current flows.

beats.narration: Wire the drain through a pull up resistor to V D D. Now a high input grounds the output through the channel; a low input lets the resistor pull V out back up. That is a logic inverter built from one transistor and one resistor.

elements.content: Inverter schematic — V_DD up top → R_D → drain; gate ← V_in; source → ground
V_in square wave on a small scope panel toggling 0 / 1
V_out square wave directly underneath, inverted
high in → low out, low in → high out — the simplest logic gate

beats.narration: Every digital chip is a city of these little switches — billions of channels opening and closing in step with a clock.

elements.content: One voltage controls one channel — and a billion channels make a CPU.
(NMOS, V_t ≈ 0.4 V on a modern process)
